info.title: REAP API
info.description:
Public REST API for REAP (multi-tenant, agentic AI for network operations).

### Identifier conventions
- **id**: UUID — canonical and used for foreign keys and writes.
- **slug**: immutable, human-readable handle (kebab-case) used in configs/URLs. Unique per scope (org) or globally (orgs).
- **name**: human-friendly display label (mutable). Do **not** use as a reference key.

## Authentication Overview

This API supports local credentials (password, passkeys), SSO (OIDC/SAML), and email-verified bootstraps
for registration/reset/invitations. The design is enumeration-resistant and minimizes clicks for the
common case (daily sign-in).

### Daily sign-ins (no emailTx required)
- **Password**: `POST /auth/password/verify` with `{ email, password }` → returns **loginTx**.
- **Passkey (email-first)**: `POST /auth/passkeys/assert` with `{ email }` → WebAuthn options + `challengeToken`
  → `POST /auth/passkeys/assert/verify` → **loginTx**.
- **Usernameless passkey** (optional): `POST /auth/passkeys/assert` with `{ usernameless: true }`.

Exchange **loginTx** at `POST /auth/token`:
- If already org-bound (SSO, single org, or server inference) → returns **TokenResponse**.
- If not org-bound and multiple orgs exist → returns **200** with `{ nextStep: "pickOrg", memberships:[...] }`.
  The server **SHOULD filter out ineligible orgs** so the client can re-call `/auth/token` with `orgId`
  without additional policy checks.
- To **switch orgs** later, call `POST /auth/token` with `grantType:"refresh"` and `orgId`.

### SSO (OIDC/SAML)
- IdP flows produce **`oidcTx`** or **`samlTx`**, which you exchange at `POST /auth/token`.
- HRD (home realm discovery): `POST /auth/discover/start` always replies **200** with a discriminated
  `nextStep`:
    - `sso_redirect` (single, safe target) — redirect using `connection.startUrl` (optionally include `login_hint`).
    - `picker` (multiple targets) — render an org/connection picker.
    - `verify_email` — prove mailbox control before revealing org/connection detail.
  *No membership/policy status leaks at Start; the rich, email-proven view is returned by `/auth/discover/verify`.*

Email verification is a common bootstrap across Discovery and Invitations. Invitation Accept returns emailTx plus
invited-org context (policy and SSO connections) without enumerating other orgs. Clients should drive UX from these fields
and exchange loginTx/oidcTx/samlTx at `/auth/token`.

### Email-verified bootstraps (keep `emailTx`)
- **Register password/passkey**, **reset password**, and **invitation acceptance** require proving email ownership.
  After `/auth/discover/verify` (or `/auth/invitations/accept`) you get **`emailTx`** for these operations or to
  obtain a limited pre-org session at `/auth/token` (for example, to create the first org).

### Enumeration resistance & security
- Return generic errors for failed sign-in; normalize response timing and apply rate-limits with small jitter.
- Avoid revealing user/org status or policy in pre-verification responses.
- Use HTTPS; set appropriate cache controls; consider device-bound refresh tokens and short-lived access tokens.

### Client authentication
REAP supports two client auth mechanisms:

- **Bearer JWT** (`Authorization: Bearer <jwt>`): short-lived, user/session tokens returned by `/auth/token`.
  Backends validate these locally via signature/claims.

- **API Key** (`X-Api-Key: <secret>`): long-lived, org-scoped secrets intended for automation (CI/CD, headless jobs).
  Keys are validated by REAP’s auth layer; they are not JWTs and should not be sent as Bearer tokens.

**Guidance**
- Prefer **Bearer JWTs** for interactive UIs and short-lived clients.
- Use **API keys** for machine-to-machine integrations; rotate or **PATCH** `expiresAt` to extend, and **DELETE** (revoke) when done.
- Assign permissions via **roles**: provide `roleIds` on create/patch; responses include `rolesResolved` for admin UX.
- Do not place API keys in URLs or logs. Keys are shown **once** on creation.

### API key return semantics
- The full API key **secret is returned only in the 201 Create response** of `/orgs/{orgId}/api-keys`.
- It is **never** returned by GET/PATCH/DELETE.
- Clients should display it once and prompt the operator to store it securely (password manager, vault).
- For subsequent requests, present the key as `X-Api-Key: <secret>`; do **not** use the Bearer scheme for API keys.

## Auth policies (overview)
- **SSO JIT (just-in-time) provisioning** can be enabled per org: SSO users can sign in without invitations.
- **Invite-only SSO** (optional): require an invitation before SSO users can join the org.
- **Local accounts** (optional): allow bootstrap/break-glass users without SSO.
- **Discover** avoids user enumeration; org memberships and sign-in options are revealed only after email verification.
- **Invitations** never expose tokens/links via API; the backend emails the invite link to the recipient.
- **Org auth policy** is a **singleton** at `/orgs/{orgId}/auth/policy` that controls JIT, invite-only SSO, and local-account allowances.
  The policy is retrieved/updated via **GET/PUT** and versioned with **ETag**.

## Discovery result (structure)
- **Local methods are global**: `DiscoverVerifyResponse.localConnections` lists user-level methods (`passkey`, `password`) available for the verified email — shown **once** in the UI.
- **SSO is per-org**: `memberships[].connections` lists **org-scoped** SSO options (`oidc`, `saml`). This array may be **empty** if the org has no SSO.
- **Policy hint**: `memberships[].policy.requiresSso` indicates that the org **requires** SSO (local login should not grant access there), even if local methods exist globally.

## Passwordless authentication (overview)
- New-user and invitation flows converge on **email verification** → short-lived **`emailTx`** (no user enumeration).
- Clients then use **Passkeys** (WebAuthn/FIDO2) to enroll a credential (attestation) or sign in (assertion).
- Successful passkey assertion yields **`loginTx`**, which is exchanged at **`POST /auth/token`** with `grantType=login_tx`.
- **Token grants** supported at `/auth/token`:
    - **authorization_code** (OIDC) via **`oidcTx`**
    - **saml2_bearer** (SAML) via **`ssoTx`**
    - **login_tx** (Passkey) via **`loginTx`**
    - **refresh_token** (rotation; optional `orgId` switch)
    - **email_tx** (bootstrap pre-org; limited to safe endpoints like creating the first org)
- **Stateless challenge** option for passkeys: options responses include a signed **`challengeToken`** that the client must echo on verify,
  allowing the server to validate the challenge/guardrails **without storing per-challenge state** (short TTL recommended).
- **Optional fast-path**: `POST /auth/passkeys/attest/verify?issueLoginTx=true` may return `loginTx` immediately after registration
  (policy permitting), otherwise the default flow is attest → assert → token.
- **Usernameless (passkey-first) sign-in**: the portal may skip email/Discover and call
  `POST /auth/passkeys/assert` with `{ "usernameless": true }`. The server returns
  `PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptions` with an empty/omitted `allowCredentials`. The browser’s
  Conditional UI prompts if a matching passkey exists; on success, the client verifies at
  `/auth/passkeys/assert/verify` to obtain `loginTx`, then exchanges at `/auth/token`.

## API response conventions
- **No envelopes**: endpoints return typed bodies directly.
- **Resources**: single GET/POST returns the resource object (composed from `ResourceBase` and `OrgScoped` when applicable).
- **Operational endpoints** (e.g., auth/token, passkeys) return typed operation results (no `ResourceBase`).
- **Lists**: return `{ items: [...], meta: { ...} }`, where each item is a full resource object and `meta` follows **PageMeta**. Responses MAY include `Link` headers (`rel="next"`, `rel="prev"`). When `meta.exactTotal` is omitted clients SHOULD treat totals as unknown and render “more available” messaging rather than fabricating counts.

### Cache-Control conventions
- **Mutable resource detail** (single GET, POST, PATCH) and every response that carries credentials, tokens, or bootstrap data sends `Cache-Control: no-store`. Browsers MUST revalidate before rendering drawers/forms so operators see their latest edits.
- **Collection/list endpoints** that back dashboards or tables may use `Cache-Control: private, max-age=15` together with `ETag` and `Link` headers. Clients SHOULD revalidate on manual refresh (If-None-Match) and treat the TTL as an upper bound.
- **Streaming/event feeds** and download endpoints for bootstrap bundles always respond with `Cache-Control: no-store`.
- If a response omits `Cache-Control`, treat it as non-cacheable.

### Identity & scoping
- Every object is keyed by `id` (UUID).
- Common audit fields come from `ResourceBase` (`createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `createdBy`, `updatedBy`).
- Multi-tenant scoping builds on `OrgScoped` (adds `orgId`); request bodies never include `orgId`—it comes from the path.

### Pagination & sorting
- Pagination via `limit` (1–200, default 50), `after`, `before`. Servers SHOULD return `Link` headers that mirror `meta.next`/`meta.prev` and include `meta.exactTotal` when a precise count is available.
- `meta.exactTotal` is OPTIONAL. When omitted it signals “total unknown”; when the repository already computes a count (e.g., `COUNT(*)`) servers SHOULD populate it.
- Sort (when supported) is a comma-separated list; prefix with `-` for descending (for example `-lastSeenAt,mgmtAddress`).

### Concurrency & caching
- Mutations return **ETag**; `PATCH`/`DELETE` require **If-Match** (mismatch → **412**).
- `GET` supports **If-None-Match** and may return **304 Not Modified**.
- Each response includes **`X-Request-Id`** for troubleshooting.

### Conditional GETs (ETag / If-None-Match)
- Servers return **ETag** headers on GETs for cache-friendly revalidation.
- Clients can send **If-None-Match** with the last seen ETag:
  - If representation is unchanged → **304 Not Modified** (no body).
  - If changed → **200 OK** with a new ETag and the latest representation.
- Recommended for frequently-polled resources (e.g., devices list, discovery runs, topology graphs).

### Error model
- Structured errors use the `Problem` schema.
- Common statuses: **400** (validation), **401/403** (auth/authz), **404** (not found), **409** (conflict), **412** (ETag mismatch), **429** (rate limit).

### Credentials model (overview)
- **Secret vs Credential vs Assignment**
  - **Secret**: write-only value + metadata (`type`, `fingerprint`, `last4`). Value is never returned.
  - **Credential**: one access **kind** (`cli_ssh`, `snmp_v2c`, `snmp_v3`, `api_rest`) with kind-specific fields that **reference Secret IDs** (e.g., SSH key, SNMP passwords, API key, mTLS certs).
  - **Credential Assignment**: routing rule that applies a **single credential** by scope (org / sites / specific devices) with optional match filters (hostname regex/prefix/suffix, labels, vendor/model).
  - Rotate a secret’s value via `POST /value` (use **If-Match** to guard against concurrent rotation).
- **Validation**
  - On create/update, the server validates that each referenced Secret ID is of the **expected SecretType** for the credential kind (mismatch → 400).
- **Resolution order (when multiple assignments match a device)**
  1. Lower `priority` first (e.g., 10 wins over 100)
  2. Narrower `scope` (device > sites > org)
  3. Most recent `updatedAt`
- **Consistency**
  - Single-resource endpoints return the resource (no envelopes).
  - List endpoints return `{ items, meta }` where `meta` follows `PageMeta` and cursors are passed via `limit/after/before`.
- **Concurrency & cache**
  - Mutations return **ETag**; `PATCH`/`DELETE` require **If-Match**.
  - `GET` supports **If-None-Match** to return **304 Not Modified** when ETag matches.

## Devices (key behaviors)

- **States** — `discovered`, `validated`, `unreachable`, `retired`, `merged` (see `DeviceState`).
- **Discovery-managed fields** (for example `vendor`, `model`, `osVersion`, `serial`, `hostname`, `firstSeenAt`, `lastSeenAt`) are **read-only** via API.
- **User-editable** fields: `displayName`, `labels` (case-insensitive keys; PATCH overwrites the map), `role` (free text, e.g. `access`, `core`, `firewall`, `wireless-ap`), `notes`.
- **Create** is allowed (beta/testing). Default list sort: `-lastSeenAt`.
- **Retire** via `PATCH` (`state=retired`). **DELETE** is hard-delete (beta convenience).
- **Merge** consolidates duplicates; merged-away device IDs subsequently return **404**.

## Edge connectivity (Connectors & Connector Clusters)

**Connectors** are lightweight agents (AMI/OVA/etc.) that establish outbound,
persistent control channels from customer sites to REAP. Connectors register
to an **Organization**, can optionally belong to a **Connector Cluster**, and
periodically report health, version, and capabilities.

**Connector Clusters** group one or more connectors for redundancy or capacity.
Clusters can be attached to **Sites** (N↔M). The API allows make-before-break
migrations: a Site can temporarily be served by multiple clusters. Backend
scheduling ensures only one active worker set manages a Site at a time.
- The attach result includes **multiAttached** to surface Sites now attached to this cluster and at least one other cluster.

**User-data (first-boot)**: each Connector exposes a one-time, short-lived
bootstrap bundle for cloud-init. Content negotiation:
- `Accept: text/cloud-config` → cloud-init YAML (default)
- `Accept: application/json` → JSON wrapper (opaque to clients)
- `Accept: application/base64+json` → base64 of the opaque JSON

One-time semantics: redeemed → **409 Conflict**, expired → **410 Gone**.
Responses SHOULD include `Cache-Control: no-store`.

**Concurrency & caching**: mutable single-resource endpoints return **ETag**
and require **If-Match** on updates/deletes. Reads MAY accept **If-None-Match**
and return **304**. Lists use pagination via `{ items, meta }` (see
`PageMeta`).

# SSO / IdP Connections
REAP supports per-organization **IdP connections** for **OIDC** and **SAML**.
- Connections are modeled as a discriminated union (`type: "oidc" | "saml"`).
- Connection **config** holds IdP metadata. Some fields are **readOnly** and computed by REAP (e.g., `redirectUris` for OIDC; `acsUrl`, `spEntityId` for SAML).
- **Concurrency:** single-resource GET returns **ETag**; **PATCH**/**DELETE** require **If-Match**.
- **Deletes** return **204 No Content**.
- **SAML IdP-initiated** sign-in can be allowed/blocked by `IdpSamlConfig.allowIdpInitiated` (default **true**).
# OIDC client authentication
- Confidential clients only: REAP supports client_secret_basic (default) and client_secret_post.
- private_key_jwt and public clients are not supported in this version.
- PKCE is supported but off by default; enable per connection via `config.enforcePkce`.

## Local password authentication (optional)
- Fits the same **email-first, enumeration-resistant** pattern: verify email → short-lived **`emailTx`**.
- Supports:
  - **Register** a password after email verification
  - **Verify** password to obtain **`loginTx`** (exchange at `/auth/token` with `grantType=loginTx`)
  - **Reset** password (email-verified), **Change** password (bearer session)
- Client sends the **clear-text password over HTTPS**; the server performs KDF hashing (e.g., **Argon2id** with per-user salt; optional application-level pepper in KMS).
- Store the **password hash (and parameters)** in the **regular user table** (not a secrets manager). If you use a **pepper**, store that pepper as a secret.
- Error hardening:
  - Same **lockout** semantics as passkeys (use **423** with a neutral error body)
  - Consistent, non-enumerating responses for all email-bound flows

tags.name: Auth
tags.description:
Authentication and token lifecycle (local credentials, SSO, email-verified bootstraps, refresh) plus the per-org **Auth Policy**.

**Handles**
- **`emailTx`** — proves email ownership (via Discover or invitation acceptance). Used for passkey and password flows and bootstrap (pre-org).
- **`loginTx`** — proves successful passkey/password verification; exchange at `/auth/token` with `grantType=loginTx`.
- **`oidcTx`** / **`samlTx`** — short-lived handles produced by the respective IdP callbacks (`/auth/oidc/callback`, `/auth/saml/acs`).

**Local credentials**
- **Password**
  - Daily sign-in: `POST /auth/password/verify` with `{ email, password }` → **loginTx**; legacy/bootstraps may send `{ emailTx, password }`.
  - Register/reset: `POST /auth/password/register` / `POST /auth/password/reset` (require `emailTx`; optional `?issueLoginTx=true`).
  - Change (authenticated): `POST /auth/password/change` (Bearer session).
- **Passkeys (WebAuthn/FIDO2)**
  - Register: `POST /auth/passkeys/attest` → options + `challengeToken`; `POST /auth/passkeys/attest/verify` → registers credential (optional `?issueLoginTx=true`).
  - Sign-in (email-first): `POST /auth/passkeys/assert` with `{ email }` → options + `challengeToken`; `POST /auth/passkeys/assert/verify` → **loginTx**.
  - Usernameless (Conditional UI): `{ "usernameless": true }`; legacy email-first may use `{ "emailTx": "..." }`.

**SSO (per-org)**
- **OIDC**: exchange `oidcTx` at `POST /auth/token` (optionally include `orgId` if the handle is not org-bound).
- **SAML**: exchange `samlTx` at `POST /auth/token`.
- HRD: `POST /auth/discover/start` always returns **200** with `nextStep`: `sso_redirect` (single target), `picker` (multiple), or `verify_email` (mailbox proof). Connections arrive as `connection` objects (see `ConnectionChoice`) with `connection.startUrl`.

**Tokens & org context**
- `POST /auth/token` supports:
  - `grantType:"loginTx"` + `loginTx` (optional `orgId`)
  - `grantType:"oidcTx"` + `oidcTx` (optional `orgId`)
  - `grantType:"samlTx"` + `samlTx`
  - `grantType:"emailTx"` + `emailTx` (pre-org, limited scope)
  - `grantType:"refresh"` + `refreshToken` (optional `orgId` to switch org)
- Responses use the **TokenIssueResult** union: either **TokenResponse** or `{ nextStep: "pickOrg", memberships: [...] }` (server SHOULD filter out ineligible orgs so the client can immediately re-call with `orgId`).

**Discovery rendering**
- Render **local** methods from `localConnections` (top of screen, once).
- Render **SSO per org** from `memberships[].connections` (OIDC/SAML buttons).
- If `memberships[].policy.requiresSso` is true and no SSO is listed, disable that org and show a hint.

**Post-login**
- `GET /auth/me` returns the current bearer’s profile and memberships.
- To switch organizations later, call `POST /auth/token` with `grantType:"refresh"` and the desired `orgId`.

tags.name: Files
tags.description:
Original uploaded or imported file resources.

Files represent source objects and may later produce derived Artifacts.
Use Files for user uploads and other original content, not for run-produced outputs.

**Auth Policy (singleton)**
- Path: `/orgs/{orgId}/auth/policy` (**GET/PUT**) with **ETag** for concurrency.
- Governs **requireInviteForSSO**, **allowLocalAccounts**, and **defaultRoleSlugsOnJIT**.

**Stateless challenge (optional)**
- Passkey options responses include `challengeToken`; clients MUST echo it on the corresponding verify call.
- Enables horizontal scaling without challenge caches; use short TTL and optionally track `jti` for strict single-use.

tags.name: Invitations
tags.description: Create, resend, revoke, and accept organization invitations. Accept returns emailTx and invited-org context (localConnections and SSO connections) to guide authentication.

tags.name: Auth Policy
tags.description:
Organization-level authentication controls (singleton at `/orgs/{orgId}/auth/policy`).
- **JIT (Just-In-Time) SSO provisioning**: allow first-time SSO users to join without invites.
- **Invite-only SSO**: require invites before SSO users can join.
- **Local accounts**: allow/disallow non-SSO users (e.g., bootstrap/break-glass).
- **Default roles on JIT**: roles to apply on first SSO login if IdP mappings grant none.
Concurrency: `PUT` requires **If-Match**; `GET` supports **If-None-Match**.

tags.name: IdP Connections
tags.description:
Create, list, fetch, update, and delete **IdP connections** (OIDC/SAML) at the **organization** level.
OIDC (confidential-only): **client_secret_basic** (default) and **client_secret_post** at the token endpoint.
`private_key_jwt` and public clients are not supported in this version. `enforcePkce` is available and defaults to **false**.
**ETag/If-Match** are used for concurrency. Deletes return **204**.

tags.name: IdP Mapping Rules
tags.description:
Map IdP claims/groups to REAP roles. Rules support ETag/If-Match for safe updates.
Deletions return **204**.

tags.name: Organizations
tags.description:
Organization (tenant) lifecycle: create, list, get, update, delete.
Single-resource responses return the Organization directly.
List responses return `{ items, meta }` with pagination.

tags.name: Sites
tags.description:
Sites represent customer locations reached via REAP connectors. Single-resource responses return the Site object directly.
Lists return `{ items, meta }` with pagination.

tags.name: Connectors
tags.description:
Connector lifecycle and bootstrap:
- Single-resource operations return the **Connector** object directly.
- Lists return `{ items, meta }` with pagination.
- **User-data** (`/orgs/{orgId}/connectors/{connectorId}/userdata`) provides
  per-connector **one-time** cloud-init bootstrap. Use `Accept` to choose
  the format (`text/cloud-config` by default). 409 = already redeemed;
  410 = expired.

Concurrency: responses include **ETag**; updates and deletes require **If-Match**.
Reads MAY accept **If-None-Match** (304 Not Modified).

tags.name: Devices
tags.description:
Inventory of network devices. Some attributes are discovery-managed and read-only via API.
- **List** returns `{ items, meta }` (pagination via `limit/after/before`).
- **Update** requires `If-Match`; allows editing user fields and setting `state=retired`.
- **Delete** is hard-delete (beta/testing convenience).
- **Merge** consolidates duplicates; merged-away IDs will return **404** thereafter.

tags.name: Endpoints
tags.description:
Inventory of reconciled endpoint attachments derived from MAC and ARP evidence.
- **List** returns the latest endpoint state as `{ items, meta }`.
- Endpoint history remains a separate Elasticsearch concern; this API exposes current state only.

tags.name: Connector Clusters
tags.description:
Manage connector groups and their site membership:
- Single-resource operations return the **ConnectorCluster** object directly.
- Lists return `{ items, meta }` with pagination.
- **Site membership** (N↔M) is managed via:
  - `POST .../sites:attach` (idempotent; requires **If-Match**)
  - `POST .../sites:detach` (idempotent; requires **If-Match**)
  - `GET  .../sites` (list sites attached to a cluster)
  - `GET  /orgs/{orgId}/sites/{siteId}/connector-clusters` (inverse list)
- Attach result includes **multiAttached** to surface Sites that, after the
  call, are attached to this cluster **and** at least one other cluster.
- Runtime **settings** (e.g., diagnostic knobs) can be included on create or update. PATCH accepts partial settings objects—omit fields you want to keep unchanged.

Concurrency: cluster membership changes return a new **ETag**. Use **If-Match**
to guard against races.

tags.name: Secrets
tags.description:
Manage opaque secret material for device access and integrations.
- **Value is write-only**: accepted on create/rotate; never returned by GET.
- Metadata includes `fingerprint` and `last4` for visual confirmation.
- Use `If-Match` with `ETag` when PATCHing metadata.

tags.name: Credentials
tags.description:
One credential = one access kind:
- **`cli_ssh`** — username + (SSH key **or** password); optional enable password; default port 22.
- **`snmp_v2c`** — read community (required), write community (optional); default port 161.
- **`snmp_v3`** — username + `securityLevel` (`noAuthNoPriv` | `authNoPriv` | `authPriv`), with auth/priv protocol + secrets as required; default port 161.
- **`api_rest`** — auth type (`api_key` | `basic` | `bearer` | `mtls`) with matching secret IDs (e.g., API key, password, bearer token, or mTLS cert/key/PKCS#12).

**Secrets are referenced, not embedded.** The server validates secret **types** against the credential kind on create/update (mismatch → 400).

**Responses:**
- Single resource: the Credential object (no envelope).
- Lists: `{ items, meta }` with pagination (`limit/after/before`).

**ETag/If-Match** are used for safe updates; `GET` supports `If-None-Match`.

tags.name: Credential Stores
tags.description:
External credential backends used by Credentials (e.g., CyberArk CCP).
- Stores are scoped to an org and selected explicitly by `cyberarkStoreId`.
- Type-specific attributes are stored in `attributes`.
- `ETag/If-Match` are used for safe updates; `GET` supports `If-None-Match`.

tags.name: Credential Assignments
tags.description:
Routing rules that apply a **single Credential** to a scope with optional filters:
- **Scope**: org-wide, specific sites (`siteIds`), or specific devices (`deviceIds`).
- **Filters (optional)**: hostname regex/prefix/suffix, device `labelsAll`, `vendorsAny`, `modelsAny`.

**Resolution order when multiple rules match a device:**
1) lower `priority`, 2) narrower `scope` (device > sites > org), 3) newer `updatedAt`.

**Responses:**
- Single resource: the Assignment object (no envelope).
- Lists: `{ items, meta }` with pagination.

**Concurrency**: `PATCH`/`DELETE` require `If-Match` (ETag); `GET` supports `If-None-Match`.

tags.name: Roles
tags.description:
Role catalog operations. The role body does not include `orgId`; org context is in the path.
System roles (`scope=system`) are global and immutable; org roles (`scope=org`) are defined per-org.
- **List** system + org roles visible in an org
- **Create/Update/Delete** org-defined roles (system roles are immutable)
- ETag-based concurrency on update/delete; pagination on list

tags.name: Memberships
tags.description:
Manage **user memberships** in an organization.

- Use **Invitations** to onboard new users.
- Use this API to **add existing users**, **adjust roles**, **suspend/reactivate**, or **remove** members.
- Add `expand=user` to inline a minimal user block in list/read responses to avoid N+1 lookups.

tags.name: API Keys
tags.description:
Org-scoped, long-lived credentials for automation. Use `X-Api-Key: <secret>` when calling APIs.
- **Creation**: `/orgs/{orgId}/api-keys` returns the `secret` **once** (201); never returned again.
- **Extension**: `PATCH /orgs/{orgId}/api-keys/{apiKeyId}` with `If-Match` to update `expiresAt` (or rename).
- **Revocation**: `DELETE /orgs/{orgId}/api-keys/{apiKeyId}` (idempotent).
- Use API keys for machine-to-machine use; prefer Bearer JWTs for end-user sessions.

tags.name: Cloud Integrations
tags.description:
Organization-scoped onboarding APIs for customer-managed cloud integrations.
REAP prepares the onboarding state and returns launch URLs for backend-owned customer setup flows.

tags.name: Discovery
tags.description:
Device discovery (jobs and runs). A **DiscoveryJob** is a long-lived configuration (site, seeds/CIDRs, optional schedule, status).
A **DiscoveryRun** is one execution of a job; only **one active run** (queued/running) is allowed per job (new starts return 409).
- Single resources return the object (no envelope).
- Lists return `{ items, meta }` (pagination via `limit/after/before`).
- Concurrency: `PATCH`/`DELETE` require `If-Match`; `GET` supports `If-None-Match`.

tags.name: MSP Delegations
tags.description:
Manage **Managed Service Provider (MSP)** access to a customer org.

### What is a Delegation?
A **Delegation** authorizes an MSP org to operate on a customer org within defined **scopes**
(e.g., read-only, incidents, ops manage). A Delegation is org-scoped (customer org in the path)
and references the **MSP org** by UUID.

### Directed vs Open invites
- **Directed invite**: Customer specifies an `mspOrgSlug` (a friendly slug like `acme-msp`).
  Only that MSP org may accept. The platform emails the MSP’s configured **delegation contacts**
  (fallback: superadmins). The invite **token is never returned by API**.
- **Open invite**: Customer omits `mspOrgSlug`. The platform emails the recipients the
  customer admin selected in the portal. The **first eligible MSP org** to accept claims the invite.

### Lifecycle
- Invite: `pending → (resend)* → (revoked|expired|used)`
- Delegation: `pending → active → (suspended ↔ active) → revoked`

**Security & privacy**
- Invite tokens are **single-use, time-bounded**, and sent via email as a link with a **URL fragment**
  (so tokens don't hit server logs). No token is ever shown via API.
- Administrative writes require `If-Match` with the latest `ETag`.
- Reads support `If-None-Match` for caching.
